text:
maria: heads up — eu-west GPU pool is showing sustained enqueued > 1200 for the last 3m, but node GPU util is only ~45%
incident-bot: alert: gpu-queue-length-high (eu-west) — threshold 500 crossed at 1841234500
alex: hmm that's classic head-of-line stall. are these large-seq chat workloads?
maria: mostly interactive chat + a few long-context eval jobs. the scheduler shows a single admission task at the front hogging 8/16 tokens of the batcher and blocking others.
oz: can you paste the scheduler admission dump?
maria: sure — snippet: 
```
AdmissionQueue: [job: 0x7f, size: 8, model: redwood-xxl, mode: on-demand, state: admitted]
AdmissionQueue: [job: 0x8a, size: 1, model: redwood-small, state: waiting]
AdmissionQueue: [job: 0x8b, size: 1, model: redwood-small, state: waiting]
WorkerPools: 12 nodes healthy, 14/32 gpus allocated
Batcher: continuous-batching enabled, max_batch_size: 16, scheduler_policy: FIFO
```
ishaan: FIFO + variable size workloads = HOL blocking. We've seen this pattern where a single large job prevents small ones from filling free slots.
alex: why is max_batch_size 16 when most jobs are tiny? config override?
maria: we recently rolled the new admission gate that tries to pack by job size but I think the comparison function has a bug: it compares job.size to queue_head.size rather than available_slots, so large jobs never yield.
oz: that matches the logs. can we hotfix to short-circuit if job.size > available_slots and try next job?
ishaan: yes — simple conditional: if job.size > available_slots then continue to next candidate. currently the loop does `if head.size <= candidate.size then swap` which is inverted.
alex: patch looks safe. however we should mitigate immediately — can we enable fair-slicing policy as a stopgap? set scheduler_policy=FAIR-SLICE in eu-west pool.
maria: applying change now to pool eu-west-1: `redwoodctl pool update eu-west-1 --scheduler-policy FAIR-SLICE`
deploy-bot: rollout started for config redwood:eu-west:scheduler-policy by maria at 1841234578
maria: config applied. monitoring...
ishaan: also temporarily lower admission max_job_size to 4 so XXL jobs get split/preempted: `admission.max_job_size=4`
oz: are we able to preempt the currently admitted large job?
maria: not without a restart of the worker process — that would drop active KV caches. prefer to let it finish since it's at ~60% progress according to task heartbeat.
alex: ok. keep an eye on latency for small jobs. can we add a short-term rate-limit exemption for small models so control plane prioritizes them?
ishaan: added a routing rule: prioritize by (model_size_category, latency_slo). small models get higher priority.
incident-bot: status update: queue length dropping to 320 at 1841234690
maria: nice. GPU util climbed to 78% after policy change — looks like fragmentation resolved.
oz: we'll push the code fix to admission comparator in <30m and ship a unit test for mixed sizes. also add a regression test that simulates alternating big/small arrivals.
alex: make sure to link to cost impact — this was causing idle GPUs with high queueing which inflates latency and reduces throughput. add to postmortem.
maria: created short incident ticket: https://redwood/ops/INC-1841 — root cause: admission comparator mis-ordering leading to HOL blocking. mitigation: FAIR-SLICE + admission.max_job_size temp limit.
ishaan: notes for longer term: consider size-aware bucketed queues + stealing, and prefer packing by available_slots. Also consider admission backoff for long-tail jobs.
oz: agreed. i'll take the patch. thanks all :thumbsup:
